extracted.intended_audience: typesetters, printers, book designers, typographers, press staff evaluating type choices
extracted.subtask_description: Compare and select typefaces and settings for book composition by inspecting printed specimens (type family, point size, leading, style variants) using continuous body text and character samples. The page shows how face, size, and line spacing affect legibility and appearance in typical book copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typeface family (face name)
rubrics_metrics.description: SPECIMENS OF TYPES IN USE — displays named type families such as MONOTYPE, CASLON OLD STYLE, SCOTCH ROMAN (face names shown as headings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specimen for visual comparison of letterforms, weight, and overall texture across faces; the page presents the same text in each face so designers can judge suitability for body text and headings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point size (six through fourteen point examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Point-size labels such as 'SIX POINT', 'SEVEN POINT', 'EIGHT POINT', 'NINE POINT', 'TEN POINT', 'ELEVEN POINT', 'TWELVE POINT', 'FOURTEEN POINT' appear with the same sample text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine the same paragraph at multiple point sizes to assess legibility, hyphenation behavior, line breaks, and overall page color; choose size appropriate to reading distance and book format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leading / line spacing: Solid vs Leaded
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens are explicitly marked '[Solid]' or '[Leaded]' before paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare 'Solid' (tight leading) and 'Leaded' (increased leading) renderings to judge readability, white-space rhythm, and density; select leading to avoid collisions or overly loose texture in body copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style variant / finish: 'Gushing' variants and specimen numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Variants labeled like 'GUSHING NO. TWENTY-FIVE' and numbered specimens (e.g., 'NO. THIRTY-ONE', 'NO. EIGHT') appear alongside face and size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These variant labels indicate specific cuts/finishes/series — compare their rendering for subtle differences in stroke, spacing, or optical adjustment; record face + variant + size when specifying composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of continuous prose (real book copy) as specimen text
rubrics_metrics.description: Each specimen uses the same excerpt of continuous prose (a passage about Polybius, Alexander, Rome) to show type 'IN USE'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer real running text (not isolated words) in specimens because it reveals hyphenation, justification, punctuation spacing, and paragraph color; designers should inspect whole-paragraph flow rather than isolated glyphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uppercase / small-caps / headings and display lines
rubrics_metrics.description: All-caps headings and emphasized lines appear (e.g., 'A WORLD-EMPIRE, INCLUDING ALL THE LANDS', 'BUT FAR MORE SERIOUS WAS THE PATENT FACT...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect display/capital settings to ensure appropriate weight and spacing at intended sizes; capitals and small-caps affect line length and visual emphasis differently than lowercase text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerals and punctuation rendering
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeral sequences '1234567890' and punctuation/ornamental sequences are included in each specimen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check numerals, figures, and punctuation for alignment, tabular vs proportional behavior, and harmony with lowercase/uppercase text; important for tables, running heads, and page numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character-sequence/kerning samples (AEIOU / aeioii etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated vowel and character clusters like 'AEIOU', 'aeiou', 'aeioii', 'deidii' are printed to show individual letterforms and pairings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use character-sequence samples to evaluate individual glyph shapes, internal counter shapes, and kerning/letterspacing across frequent letter combinations; helpful for spotting awkward pairs or spacing inconsistencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen cataloging: label face + size + variant
rubrics_metrics.description: Each specimen block is labeled with face, point size and a series/number (e.g., 'MONOTYPE — TEN POINT NO. THIRTY-ONE [Solid]'), and sometimes with style notes ('[Leaded]').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When specifying type for production, record the face name, point size, series/number, and whether the setting is leaded or solid so printers can reproduce the intended appearance exactly.
